content.text:
The campaign is finished. I submitted **index 115** (Fe 0.32, Ni 0.18, V 0.50), which gave the highest photocurrent of the three samples I measured: **2.1×10⁻⁷ A**. With only three measurements across 200 compositions, I can't say whether this is close to the best in the library.

**Photocurrent results (3 of 3 used):**

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 115 | 0.32 / 0.18 / 0.50 | **2.1×10⁻⁷ A** |
| 136 | 0.45 / 0.19 / 0.36 | 7×10⁻⁸ A |
| 13 | 0.12 / 0.19 / 0.69 | 0 |

**XRD results (5 of 5 used):**
- **Middle of the library** (indices 122 and 130): the same crystal structure appears in both, with peaks at Q ≈ 2.455, 2.858, 4.06 and 4.80 Å⁻¹.
- **Most V-rich sample** (index 13): that structure plus an extra phase with low-angle peaks. This sample gave no photocurrent.
- **Fe-rich and Ni-rich corners** (indices 145 and 56): a different structure, with peaks at Q ≈ 2.67 and 4.50 Å⁻¹.

**How I read it:** photocurrent needs a fair amount of Fe. It peaked at a middling Fe:V ratio (about 0.65 at index 115) and fell off when I moved toward more Fe. I didn't measure photocurrent in the Fe-rich or Ni-rich corners, so I can't rule them out.
